method.label: How a setup earns its place
method.note: The whole-picture method behind this brief, in plain English, sits under every setup brief on the terminal.

rows.label: Independent strategy families agreeing

rows.label: Tensor pattern engine confirms a swing

rows.label: Tensor dip context (no confirmed swing)

rows.label: ChartsLector strength (context only)

rows.label: The desk actually entered today
rows.note: A filled entry is the desk's revealed conviction and outranks an evaluated intent. A position the desk already holds earns the same credit — the money is committed either way (DA-2: one entered predicate — fills today, an entry-dated record today, or a current holding, options holdings mapped to their underlying). Doctrine supports the idea; the number is desk-set.

rows.label: A strategy tried to enter and was turned away
rows.note: Paid only when the broker's own rejection says the account could not fund the order (buying power). A rejection for any other reason earns nothing.

rows.label: Fear day — dip-habitat family
rows.note: Departure, recorded: the DIP spec's fear bonus is +10 (Component 1), paid inside a dip-depth component this rubric does not compute. The desk merges fear into this single regime factor and sets the dip-family credit at 8. The fear-day gate itself follows the spec — SPY down more than 1.5% or VIX up more than 15% (desk extensions: VIX at 25 or higher, or a red index day with VIX at 20 or higher).

rows.label: Fear day — other family
rows.note: A smaller credit: fear days are the dip buyers' validated habitat rather than this family's.

rows.label: Uptrend — momentum family
rows.note: The DIP spec's market-context component pays 10 in an uptrend and 0 in a downtrend, without splitting by family. The desk splits by family habitat (the 2026-10-13 ruling: swing signals do well in bearish regimes) and sets its own numbers.

rows.label: Uptrend — dip family
rows.note: The desk's method buys dips inside uptrends, not against them. Desk-set number; see the uptrend note above.

rows.label: Downtrend — reversal-class family
rows.note: Only reversal-class setups keep support in a downtrend. Desk-set number; the DIP spec's context component pays 0 in a downtrend and does not make this exception — the desk's bearish-habitat ruling (2026-10-13) does.

rows.label: Downtrend — other family
rows.note: Trend-following entries are penalised until the regime turns. Desk-set number.

rows.label: Chop (sideways) market
rows.note: No tailwind either way; the setup stands on its own evidence. Desk-set number.

rows.label: Reset at support — at the 20-day average
rows.note: Paid only when the close is within 1% of the 20-day average — the tolerance the spec itself sets.

rows.label: Reset near support — wider pullback
rows.note: A wider, weaker condition the desk credits at half the spec route: the close within about a day's range of the 20-day average, or reset onto the recent swing-low zone. Desk-set.

rows.label: Stop distance 1.5-2.5x the daily range
rows.note: The distance bands follow the desk's chart-reading method — stops at least 1.5x the daily range, 1.5-2.5x preferred. The point values are desk-set.

rows.label: Stop distance 2.5-4x the daily range
rows.note: Wider than the ideal band, so the position must ride out more noise. Desk-set points; band per the chart-reading method.

rows.label: Stop distance 1-1.5x the daily range
rows.note: Below the method's 1.5x floor — noise can shake it out. Desk-set points.

rows.label: Stop inside one day's range
rows.note: A stop inside the normal daily range is very likely to be noise-stopped, so it deducts. Desk-set points.

rows.label: Stop distance beyond 4x the daily range
rows.note: The level is defined, but a great deal of room sits between entry and exit. Desk-set points.

rows.label: Parabolic-spike guard (up 25% or more in 10 sessions)
rows.note: Not a flat deduction: when a name has run 25% or more in 10 sessions, the whole finished score is multiplied by 0.7 — the first red day of a spike is not the buy.

rows.label: Stretched (up 15-25% in 10 sessions)
rows.note: A lesser extension warning below the spike line. Desk-set; the spec has no such tier.

rows.label: Far above the 20-day average
rows.note: Close more than 2.5x the daily range above the 20-day average — poor initiation quality even when the trend is intact. Desk-set.

rows.label: Broken structure (closed below the swing low)
rows.note: Broken structure is one of the desk's named invalidators (2026-10-13 ruling: extension, no reset at support, broken structure). The point value is desk-set.

method.label: How a setup earns its place

rows.label: Independent strategy families agreeing
rows.note: The doctrine that independent families each get one vote is the Grand Synthesis (Part V). The point steps are desk-set: the synthesis gives no numbers, and the DIP spec's 30-point block is a different quantity (level confluence), so it is not borrowed here.

rows.label: Tensor pattern engine confirms a swing
rows.note: The spec grades Tensor evidence by freshness: a fresh trade signal 8 of 15, a fresh watch 4, a stale signal (4-10 sessions) 2. The desk maps those proportions onto its own scale, where the fresh weight is 14.

rows.label: Tensor dip context (no confirmed swing)
rows.note: Tensor's dip sleeve selected the name without a confirmed swing trade signal — half the fresh confirmation weight, the spec's fresh-watch proportion.

rows.label: ChartsLector strength (context only)
rows.note: A context layer: it can add points but never creates a setup (Grand Synthesis, Part V). The tier numbers are desk-set. When the ranks are more than 3 sessions old, the points are halved.

rows.label: The desk actually entered today
rows.note: A filled entry is the desk's revealed conviction and outranks an evaluated intent. A position the desk already holds earns the same credit — the money is committed either way (DA-2: one entered predicate — fills today, an entry-dated record today, or a current holding, options holdings mapped to their underlying). Doctrine supports the idea; the number is desk-set.

rows.label: A strategy tried to enter and was turned away
rows.note: Paid only when the broker's own rejection says the account could not fund the order (buying power). A rejection for any other reason earns nothing.

rows.label: Fear day — dip-habitat family
rows.note: Departure, recorded: the DIP spec's fear bonus is +10 (Component 1), paid inside a dip-depth component this rubric does not compute. The desk merges fear into this single regime factor and sets the dip-family credit at 8. The fear-day gate itself follows the spec — SPY down more than 1.5% or VIX up more than 15% (desk extensions: VIX at 25 or higher, or a red index day with VIX at 20 or higher).

rows.label: Fear day — other family
rows.note: A smaller credit: fear days are the dip buyers' validated habitat rather than this family's.

rows.label: Uptrend — momentum family
rows.note: The DIP spec's market-context component pays 10 in an uptrend and 0 in a downtrend, without splitting by family. The desk splits by family habitat (the 2026-10-13 ruling: swing signals do well in bearish regimes) and sets its own numbers.

rows.label: Uptrend — dip family
rows.note: The desk's method buys dips inside uptrends, not against them. Desk-set number; see the uptrend note above.

rows.label: Downtrend — reversal-class family
rows.note: Only reversal-class setups keep support in a downtrend. Desk-set number; the DIP spec's context component pays 0 in a downtrend and does not make this exception — the desk's bearish-habitat ruling (2026-10-13) does.

rows.label: Downtrend — other family
rows.note: Trend-following entries are penalised until the regime turns. Desk-set number.

rows.label: Chop (sideways) market
rows.note: No tailwind either way; the setup stands on its own evidence. Desk-set number.

rows.label: Reset at support — at the 20-day average
rows.note: Paid only when the close is within 1% of the 20-day average — the tolerance the spec itself sets.

rows.label: Reset near support — wider pullback
rows.note: A wider, weaker condition the desk credits at half the spec route: the close within about a day's range of the 20-day average, or reset onto the recent swing-low zone. Desk-set.

rows.label: Stop distance 1.5-2.5x the daily range
rows.note: The distance bands follow the desk's chart-reading method — stops at least 1.5x the daily range, 1.5-2.5x preferred. The point values are desk-set.

rows.label: Stop distance 2.5-4x the daily range
rows.note: Wider than the ideal band, so the position must ride out more noise. Desk-set points; band per the chart-reading method.

rows.label: Stop distance 1-1.5x the daily range
rows.note: Below the method's 1.5x floor — noise can shake it out. Desk-set points.

rows.label: Stop inside one day's range
rows.note: A stop inside the normal daily range is very likely to be noise-stopped, so it deducts. Desk-set points.

rows.label: Stop distance beyond 4x the daily range
rows.note: The level is defined, but a great deal of room sits between entry and exit. Desk-set points.

rows.label: Parabolic-spike guard (up 25% or more in 10 sessions)
rows.note: Not a flat deduction: when a name has run 25% or more in 10 sessions, the whole finished score is multiplied by 0.7 — the first red day of a spike is not the buy.

rows.label: Stretched (up 15-25% in 10 sessions)
rows.note: A lesser extension warning below the spike line. Desk-set; the spec has no such tier.

rows.label: Far above the 20-day average
rows.note: Close more than 2.5x the daily range above the 20-day average — poor initiation quality even when the trend is intact. Desk-set.

rows.label: Broken structure (closed below the swing low)
rows.note: Broken structure is one of the desk's named invalidators (2026-10-13 ruling: extension, no reset at support, broken structure). The point value is desk-set.

method.label: How a setup earns its place
method.note: The whole-picture method behind this brief, in plain English, sits under every setup brief on the terminal.

rows.label: Independent strategy families agreeing
rows.note: The doctrine that independent families each get one vote is the Grand Synthesis (Part V). The point steps are desk-set: the synthesis gives no numbers, and the DIP spec's 30-point block is a different quantity (level confluence), so it is not borrowed here.

rows.label: Tensor pattern engine confirms a swing
rows.note: The spec grades Tensor evidence by freshness: a fresh trade signal 8 of 15, a fresh watch 4, a stale signal (4-10 sessions) 2. The desk maps those proportions onto its own scale, where the fresh weight is 14.

rows.label: Tensor dip context (no confirmed swing)
rows.note: Tensor's dip sleeve selected the name without a confirmed swing trade signal — half the fresh confirmation weight, the spec's fresh-watch proportion.

rows.label: ChartsLector strength (context only)
rows.note: A context layer: it can add points but never creates a setup (Grand Synthesis, Part V). The tier numbers are desk-set. When the ranks are more than 3 sessions old, the points are halved.

rows.label: The desk actually entered today
rows.note: A filled entry is the desk's revealed conviction and outranks an evaluated intent. A position the desk already holds earns the same credit — the money is committed either way (DA-2: one entered predicate — fills today, an entry-dated record today, or a current holding, options holdings mapped to their underlying). Doctrine supports the idea; the number is desk-set.

rows.label: A strategy tried to enter and was turned away
rows.note: Paid only when the broker's own rejection says the account could not fund the order (buying power). A rejection for any other reason earns nothing.

rows.label: Fear day — dip-habitat family
rows.note: Departure, recorded: the DIP spec's fear bonus is +10 (Component 1), paid inside a dip-depth component this rubric does not compute. The desk merges fear into this single regime factor and sets the dip-family credit at 8. The fear-day gate itself follows the spec — SPY down more than 1.5% or VIX up more than 15% (desk extensions: VIX at 25 or higher, or a red index day with VIX at 20 or higher).

rows.label: Fear day — other family
rows.note: A smaller credit: fear days are the dip buyers' validated habitat rather than this family's.

rows.label: Uptrend — momentum family

method.label: How a setup earns its place
method.note: The whole-picture method behind this brief, in plain English, sits under every setup brief on the terminal.

rows.label: Independent strategy families agreeing
rows.note: The doctrine that independent families each get one vote is the Grand Synthesis (Part V). The point steps are desk-set: the synthesis gives no numbers, and the DIP spec's 30-point block is a different quantity (level confluence), so it is not borrowed here.

rows.label: Tensor pattern engine confirms a swing
rows.note: The spec grades Tensor evidence by freshness: a fresh trade signal 8 of 15, a fresh watch 4, a stale signal (4-10 sessions) 2. The desk maps those proportions onto its own scale, where the fresh weight is 14.

rows.label: Tensor dip context (no confirmed swing)
rows.note: Tensor's dip sleeve selected the name without a confirmed swing trade signal — half the fresh confirmation weight, the spec's fresh-watch proportion.

rows.label: ChartsLector strength (context only)
rows.note: A context layer: it can add points but never creates a setup (Grand Synthesis, Part V). The tier numbers are desk-set. When the ranks are more than 3 sessions old, the points are halved.

rows.label: The desk actually entered today
rows.note: A filled entry is the desk's revealed conviction and outranks an evaluated intent. A position the desk already holds earns the same credit — the money is committed either way (DA-2: one entered predicate — fills today, an entry-dated record today, or a current holding, options holdings mapped to their underlying). Doctrine supports the idea; the number is desk-set.

rows.label: A strategy tried to enter and was turned away
rows.note: Paid only when the broker's own rejection says the account could not fund the order (buying power). A rejection for any other reason earns nothing.

rows.label: Fear day — dip-habitat family
rows.note: Departure, recorded: the DIP spec's fear bonus is +10 (Component 1), paid inside a dip-depth component this rubric does not compute. The desk merges fear into this single regime factor and sets the dip-family credit at 8. The fear-day gate itself follows the spec — SPY down more than 1.5% or VIX up more than 15% (desk extensions: VIX at 25 or higher, or a red index day with VIX at 20 or higher).

rows.label: Fear day — other family
rows.note: A smaller credit: fear days are the dip buyers' validated habitat rather than this family's.

rows.label: Uptrend — momentum family
rows.note: The DIP spec's market-context component pays 10 in an uptrend and 0 in a downtrend, without splitting by family. The desk splits by family habitat (the 2026-10-13 ruling: swing signals do well in bearish regimes) and sets its own numbers.

rows.label: Uptrend — dip family
rows.note: The desk's method buys dips inside uptrends, not against them. Desk-set number; see the uptrend note above.

rows.label: Downtrend — reversal-class family
rows.note: Only reversal-class setups keep support in a downtrend. Desk-set number; the DIP spec's context component pays 0 in a downtrend and does not make this exception — the desk's bearish-habitat ruling (2026-10-13) does.

rows.label: Downtrend — other family
rows.note: Trend-following entries are penalised until the regime turns. Desk-set number.

rows.label: Chop (sideways) market
rows.note: No tailwind either way; the setup stands on its own evidence. Desk-set number.

rows.label: Reset at support — at the 20-day average
rows.note: Paid only when the close is within 1% of the 20-day average — the tolerance the spec itself sets.

rows.label: Reset near support — wider pullback
rows.note: A wider, weaker condition the desk credits at half the spec route: the close within about a day's range of the 20-day average, or reset onto the recent swing-low zone. Desk-set.

rows.label: Stop distance 1.5-2.5x the daily range
rows.note: The distance bands follow the desk's chart-reading method — stops at least 1.5x the daily range, 1.5-2.5x preferred. The point values are desk-set.

rows.label: Stop distance 2.5-4x the daily range
rows.note: Wider than the ideal band, so the position must ride out more noise. Desk-set points; band per the chart-reading method.

rows.label: Stop distance 1-1.5x the daily range
rows.note: Below the method's 1.5x floor — noise can shake it out. Desk-set points.

rows.label: Stop inside one day's range
rows.note: A stop inside the normal daily range is very likely to be noise-stopped, so it deducts. Desk-set points.

rows.label: Stop distance beyond 4x the daily range
rows.note: The level is defined, but a great deal of room sits between entry and exit. Desk-set points.

rows.label: Parabolic-spike guard (up 25% or more in 10 sessions)
rows.note: Not a flat deduction: when a name has run 25% or more in 10 sessions, the whole finished score is multiplied by 0.7 — the first red day of a spike is not the buy.

rows.label: Stretched (up 15-25% in 10 sessions)
rows.note: A lesser extension warning below the spike line. Desk-set; the spec has no such tier.

rows.label: Far above the 20-day average
rows.note: Close more than 2.5x the daily range above the 20-day average — poor initiation quality even when the trend is intact. Desk-set.

rows.label: Broken structure (closed below the swing low)
rows.note: Broken structure is one of the desk's named invalidators (2026-10-13 ruling: extension, no reset at support, broken structure). The point value is desk-set.

rows.note: The spec grades Tensor evidence by freshness: a fresh trade signal 8 of 15, a fresh watch 4, a stale signal (4-10 sessions) 2. The desk maps those proportions onto its own scale, where the fresh weight is 14.

rows.label: Tensor dip context (no confirmed swing)
rows.note: Tensor's dip sleeve selected the name without a confirmed swing trade signal — half the fresh confirmation weight, the spec's fresh-watch proportion.

rows.label: ChartsLector strength (context only)
rows.note: A context layer: it can add points but never creates a setup (Grand Synthesis, Part V). The tier numbers are desk-set. When the ranks are more than 3 sessions old, the points are halved.

rows.label: The desk actually entered today
rows.note: A filled entry is the desk's revealed conviction and outranks an evaluated intent. A position the desk already holds earns the same credit — the money is committed either way (DA-2: one entered predicate — fills today, an entry-dated record today, or a current holding, options holdings mapped to their underlying). Doctrine supports the idea; the number is desk-set.

rows.label: A strategy tried to enter and was turned away
rows.note: Paid only when the broker's own rejection says the account could not fund the order (buying power). A rejection for any other reason earns nothing.

rows.label: Fear day — dip-habitat family
rows.note: Departure, recorded: the DIP spec's fear bonus is +10 (Component 1), paid inside a dip-depth component this rubric does not compute. The desk merges fear into this single regime factor and sets the dip-family credit at 8. The fear-day gate itself follows the spec — SPY down more than 1.5% or VIX up more than 15% (desk extensions: VIX at 25 or higher, or a red index day with VIX at 20 or higher).

rows.label: Fear day — other family
rows.note: A smaller credit: fear days are the dip buyers' validated habitat rather than this family's.

rows.label: Uptrend — momentum family
rows.note: The DIP spec's market-context component pays 10 in an uptrend and 0 in a downtrend, without splitting by family. The desk splits by family habitat (the 2026-10-13 ruling: swing signals do well in bearish regimes) and sets its own numbers.

rows.label: Uptrend — dip family
rows.note: The desk's method buys dips inside uptrends, not against them. Desk-set number; see the uptrend note above.

rows.label: Downtrend — reversal-class family
rows.note: Only reversal-class setups keep support in a downtrend. Desk-set number; the DIP spec's context component pays 0 in a downtrend and does not make this exception — the desk's bearish-habitat ruling (2026-10-13) does.

rows.label: Downtrend — other family
rows.note: Trend-following entries are penalised until the regime turns. Desk-set number.

rows.label: Chop (sideways) market
rows.note: No tailwind either way; the setup stands on its own evidence. Desk-set number.

rows.label: Reset at support — at the 20-day average
rows.note: Paid only when the close is within 1% of the 20-day average — the tolerance the spec itself sets.

rows.label: Reset near support — wider pullback
rows.note: A wider, weaker condition the desk credits at half the spec route: the close within about a day's range of the 20-day average, or reset onto the recent swing-low zone. Desk-set.

rows.label: Stop distance 1.5-2.5x the daily range
rows.note: The distance bands follow the desk's chart-reading method — stops at least 1.5x the daily range, 1.5-2.5x preferred. The point values are desk-set.

rows.label: Stop distance 2.5-4x the daily range
rows.note: Wider than the ideal band, so the position must ride out more noise. Desk-set points; band per the chart-reading method.

rows.label: Stop distance 1-1.5x the daily range
rows.note: Below the method's 1.5x floor — noise can shake it out. Desk-set points.

rows.label: Stop inside one day's range
rows.note: A stop inside the normal daily range is very likely to be noise-stopped, so it deducts. Desk-set points.

rows.label: Stop distance beyond 4x the daily range
rows.note: The level is defined, but a great deal of room sits between entry and exit. Desk-set points.

rows.label: Parabolic-spike guard (up 25% or more in 10 sessions)
rows.note: Not a flat deduction: when a name has run 25% or more in 10 sessions, the whole finished score is multiplied by 0.7 — the first red day of a spike is not the buy.

rows.label: Stretched (up 15-25% in 10 sessions)
rows.note: A lesser extension warning below the spike line. Desk-set; the spec has no such tier.

rows.label: Far above the 20-day average
rows.note: Close more than 2.5x the daily range above the 20-day average — poor initiation quality even when the trend is intact. Desk-set.

rows.label: Broken structure (closed below the swing low)
rows.note: Broken structure is one of the desk's named invalidators (2026-10-13 ruling: extension, no reset at support, broken structure). The point value is desk-set.
